## TL;DR

Release cuts on the Releases page now show the same shared `ActivityIndicator` as task cards while `/api/release/run` reports `state: running`: on the “Releasing…” pill, beside the “View progress” control, and on the cut drawer’s step heading. Preview capture uses a new `release:cutRunning` shot fixture. Tests cover running vs terminal run states.

## Work and rationale

Long release cuts looked frozen because the pill and progress block were static text. The fix reuses `ActivityIndicator` and `useActivityMotion` from #1062 with no new animation settings.

The UI gates indicators on the existing `running` ref, which already tracks live poll results and POST responses. Three mount points mirror task surfaces: header pill, primary CTA when relabelled to “View progress”, and the drawer’s `phaseHeading` line.

Capture needed a deterministic run snapshot. Following #1071’s email fixture pattern, `shotFixtureReleaseRun()` pins step 4 (“checking”) with sample log text. `applyReleaseRunFixture()` runs on mount and short-circuits `pollRun()` so preview ticks do not clear the pin. The `/releases?drawer=cut` deep link still opens the panel for drawer shots.

Layout: flex on `.rel-pill`, `.rel-cut-open`, and `.release-progress-heading` so the sized artwork aligns with labels without changing card height.

## Approaches tried

Initial idea was a release-specific animation; dropped because the task forbids new motion code. Considered only the drawer heading; acceptance also requires the page pill and View progress row.

## Challenges and blockers

None in implementation. Declared shots were written via `repoos api PATCH` because CLI `repoos update` targeted the main checkout; the worktree task file was synced manually with the same JSON.

## Key learnings

Release run state is already centralized in `running` and `run`; wiring indicators there keeps poll semantics (#0621/#0622) intact. Shot fixtures that replace poll-backed API state should return early in the poll function, not only on mount, or later ticks overwrite the capture.
